context.requirement_text: Re-check of REQ-219's design after rework iteration 2 (see prior iteration-1 FAIL handoff's context.requirement_text for the full requirement description, unchanged since then).

task.description: CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR (WF-02 Step 1b) RE-CHECK, rework iteration 2, for REQ-219: verify CODE-DESIGNER's two targeted fixes (AC2 cold-boot test mechanism; compile_env double-gate for pollers_init_probe/force_poller_crash) actually resolve the iteration-1 FAIL, and re-confirm all 10 ACs plus no-implementation-code and ordering-constraint invariants.

checks_performed.ac2_cold_boot_mechanism: PASS -- traced §4.3's procedure step by step independently. Application.stop(:letflow) is a real, synchronous, full OTP application stop: it terminates the application master's top supervisor (Letflow.Supervisor, the actual process Letflow.Application.start/2 registers) and everything transitively under it, including Letflow.Supervisor.Infrastructure and Obs.Alerts.TaskSupervisor -- Process.whereis/1 is guaranteed nil immediately after, confirmed against real OTP semantics (Application.stop/1 does not return until application_controller has finished terminating the app's master process tree). Application.ensure_all_started(:letflow), since :letflow is not currently running, calls Application.start/2 again for real -- ecto_sql/bandit/etc. are already-started sibling apps and are skipped by ensure_all_started's own semantics (only not-yet-running apps in the dependency closure are (re)started), matching the design's own claim in step 4. This genuinely re-runs Letflow.Application.start/2's real Supervisor.start_link(children, ...) call with whatever 3-element order §2 currently specifies -- not a targeted single-child restart. Counterfactual verified independently for both orderings: correct order ([Infrastructure, Pollers, Http]) -- Infrastructure's init/1 (17 children including Obs.Alerts.TaskSupervisor last) must return {:ok, pid} before Supervisor.start_link/2 starts child 2 (Pollers), so the probe inside Pollers.init/1 observes a live pid; swapped order ([Pollers, Infrastructure, Http]) -- Pollers is child 1, so its init/1 (and the probe) runs before Infrastructure has started at all, observing nil and failing the assertion. This is a genuine, real trace of Supervisor's own sequential single-child-at-a-time startup contract, not asserted by fiat, and it correctly discriminates the exact regression AC2 exists to catch -- the flaw identified in iteration 1 (probing an already-fully-booted app, where Infrastructure's prior-boot registration masks a swapped order) is closed by tearing the whole tree down first.
checks_performed.ac2_test_isolation_safety: PASS, not left open as a load-bearing gap -- the harder question this re-check was tasked to scrutinize (whether stopping/restarting the whole :letflow OTP app mid-suite is safe for Ecto sandbox ownership and concurrent tests) is NOT left to ELIXIR-DEV/TEST-RUNNER to discover; §4.3's preamble explicitly specifies `async: false` for the new test file and explicitly invokes the same ExUnit scheduling guarantee (all async: true modules complete before any async: false module starts, and async: false modules run strictly one at a time) that test/support/admission_test_helpers.ex's own moduledoc already relies on and that this codebase has already accepted as sound for a lighter-weight single-singleton restart. Under that real ExUnit guarantee, no other test module -- sync or async -- is running concurrently while this test's Application.stop(:letflow)/ensure_all_started(:letflow) executes, so no other process's Sandbox checkout against Letflow.Repo can be in flight when Repo itself is torn down and restarted. This resolves the safety concern at design time via an explicit, verifiable mechanism (async: false + documented existing ExUnit contract), not an unverified assumption. Only the narrower, genuinely non-blocking Q4 (:logger.add_primary_filter/2's exact behavior on a duplicate id -- raise vs. ignored error tuple) is left for empirical confirmation, and the design's own defensive :logger.remove_primary_filter/1 step in §4.3 step 3 is correct and safe regardless of that answer (a no-op removal-then-readd is not a hazard either way) -- appropriately left open since it does not gate correctness.
checks_performed.logger_duplicate_filter_workaround: ACCEPTABLE -- :logger.remove_primary_filter(:letflow_secrets_redaction) before the restart, so the restart's own :logger.add_primary_filter/2 call is a genuine first-time registration again, sidesteps the question of whether a duplicate-id call raises or returns an ignored error, entirely by construction. Leaving the underlying OTP/logger behavior itself unverified (Q4) is fine for a design gate given the mitigation makes the answer immaterial to correctness -- this is exactly the kind of open question that does not block ELIXIR-DEV (both possible answers lead to the same safe outcome), unlike iteration 1's AC2 flaw which did not have this property.
checks_performed.compile_env_double_gate_fidelity: PASS -- independently re-read lib/letflow/repository/activation.ex lines 226-247: @activation_test_hooks_enabled? is resolved via Application.compile_env(:letflow, :activation_test_hooks_enabled?, false), default false, gating a functional clause additionally to a runtime opt; config/test.exs:209 confirmed to set `config :letflow, activation_test_hooks_enabled?: true` exactly as the design claims (present, true, predates this requirement per its own REQ-203 comment at lines 200-209). The design's §4.2 (@supervisor_test_hooks_enabled?) and §5.1 (@poller_test_hooks_enabled?) attributes are each a byte-for-byte-shaped Application.compile_env/3 call against this exact existing key, correctly modeled on the real precedent, not a paraphrase.
checks_performed.key_reuse_judgment: ACCEPTABLE, not a blocking defect -- re-read AC7's literal text: 'config/test.exs, config/dev.exs and config/prod.exs need no changes.' A new :supervisor_test_hooks_enabled? key would require a new line in config/test.exs, which is a change to that file under AC7's own literal wording (AC7 does not say 'no changes to the three existing gate keys' scoped narrowly -- it says the three FILES need no changes, full stop). Reusing the already-present, already-true :activation_test_hooks_enabled? key is therefore not merely a stylistic convenience but the only way to satisfy both the double-gate precedent AND AC7's literal bar simultaneously, and the design says so explicitly rather than silently choosing it. The semantic-coupling risk named in this re-check's brief (disabling activation test hooks for an unrelated reason would silently also disable these; a future grep for 'activation' would not surface these two unrelated call sites) is real but non-fatal: it is explicitly disclosed in three places (§4.2, §5.1, §7) as a REVIEWER-facing checklist item with a concrete named exit path (rename to a generic key once a third consumer appears), and it does not create any ambiguity for ELIXIR-DEV to resolve two different ways -- the exact shape of both attributes is fully pinned down. This is a legitimate, disclosed design trade-off for REVIEWER to bless or reject at WF-02 Step 2d, not an unresolved gap that should block the design gate.
checks_performed.all_10_acs_covered: PASS -- re-verified fresh against docs/requirements.yaml REQ-219 lines 13077-13086: AC1 (exactly 3 top-level children, :one_for_one) -> §2; AC2 (Infrastructure-before-Pollers list order + dedicated whereis-during-init test) -> §4 (mechanism now sound, see above); AC3 (17-child Infrastructure list, exact order, ISS-0224) -> §1.1 (unchanged from previously-PASSed content); AC4 (Pollers owns exactly the 2 gated pollers, empty-list-ok) -> §1.2/§6; AC5 (crash-loop isolation, Repo pid unchanged, test-backed) -> §3/§5 (Repo-pid-unchanged assertion present at §5 step 5); AC6 (Http owns exactly Bandit) -> §1.3; AC7 (no config file changes) -> §4.2/§5.1/§7, holds under the key-reuse decision; AC8 (Pollers moduledoc records override+rationale verbatim) -> §3/§7; AC9 (REVIEWER sign-off content: ordering guarantees, InstanceSupervisor placement, :one_for_one-vs-:rest_for_one justification) -> §7's explicit checklist; AC10 (mix test/mix compile --warnings-as-errors, real output) -> correctly left to ELIXIR-DEV/TEST-RUNNER as a build-time artifact, not a design-time one.
checks_performed.ordering_constraints_unchanged: PASS -- §1.1's ISS-0224 (SandboxPool.TaskSupervisor before SandboxPool) and ISS-0429 (Obs.Alerts.TaskSupervisor last in Infrastructure, supervisor-boundary guarantee) content is materially identical to the iteration-1 text CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR already PASSed; only §4's AC2 mechanism and §4.2/§5.1's gating changed, per the rework's own scope.
checks_performed.no_implementation_code: PASS -- no fenced code blocks anywhere in the file (grep for ``` returns nothing). The only fn-shaped fragments are two small anonymous-function expressions embedded in §4.3's prose test-procedure narration (the pollers_init_probe closure and an on_exit closure), consistent with the already-accepted req218-style convention of describing test procedures as prose steps with inline expressions rather than defmodule/def function bodies for PRODUCTION code -- no module implementation (Letflow.Supervisor.Infrastructure/Pollers/Http, or the Poller guard clause) is written as a real function body anywhere; every production-facing element remains a bare child-spec tuple, module attribute expression, or keyword list, exactly as iteration 1's already-accepted no_implementation_code check found.
